guia.what: Picks a value within a continuous range, from a list of stops (`data-ts-slider-values`), or a span with two thumbs that can’t cross (`data-ts-slider-range`). It’s built on native `<input type="range">` elements, so dragging and keyboard behavior come from the browser. It can show the current value and the min/max marks, run vertically (`is-vertical`), or be read-only.
whenUse: The value is approximate and visual feedback on the range helps (volume, opacity, a threshold).
Where the value sits in the range matters more than the exact number.
Dragging to adjust feels more natural than typing.
You filter by a span (price, usage quota, a range of deployment dates). Use `data-ts-slider-range`, with two thumbs.
The possible values follow an uneven scale (plan seats: 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250). `data-ts-slider-values` lists the stops, and the control only lands on them.
whenAvoid: The range is huge and dragging is imprecise → `number-input`.
It’s a few discrete options (Free, Pro, Enterprise) → `segmented-control`.
dos: Show the current value and the end marks for reference.
With stops, give each one its text (`data-ts-slider-format` or `data-ts-slider-texts`). The screen reader says “6 px, Suave,” not a position.
Pick a `step` that doesn’t frustrate—neither too fine nor too coarse.
Save or fetch data when the value is committed. `ts:commit` fires on release; `ts:change` fires on every movement.
Use `aria-readonly="true"` on the input, not `disabled`, when the value is shown and submitted with the form but can’t be edited.
donts: Don’t use it when precision matters and mistakes are costly.
Don’t hide the value. Without a number, the user is guessing.
Don’t send a request for every change during a drag.

teclado.action: Adjusts the value by `step` (in RTL, the right arrow decreases it, like the native input).
Same as the horizontal arrows. When vertical, ↑ moves toward the maximum.
Goes to the minimum or the maximum. With `is-range`, the start handle stops at the end handle and vice versa.
Jumps several steps, like the native input. With stops (`data-ts-slider-values`), it moves one stop, or a tenth of the list when there are more than 14.
With `is-range`, moves through both handles (start, then end).

nucleo: It uses a native `<input type="range">` for dragging and the keyboard. Core adds the track fill, the `range` handle limits, and the events. On every move, Core updates the fill, `aria-valuenow`, each handle’s ARIA limits, and the value text. `range` handles don’t cross, and when they overlap, the one with room to move stays on top. Clicking or dragging on the rail moves the nearest handle. `form.reset()` repaints the fill.
